topics.title: A spy story: clues and conditionals

learn.hook: A spy who is fat, ordinary-looking and carries no gadgets. Can he still win?
points: 'The Midnight Visitor' by Robert Arthur features Ausable, a secret agent who looks nothing like the glamorous spies of films; a young writer, Fowler, is disappointed by him.
In Ausable's room they find Max, a rival agent with a pistol, who has come for an important secret paper.
Spy stories have secret missions, suspense, clues and a twist at the end.
Conditionals: first conditional for a real possibility (If + present, will + verb): 'If the police come, they will search the room.'
Second conditional for an imaginary situation (If + past, would + verb): 'If I were a spy, I would carry a camera.' Use 'were' for all persons in formal English.

example.q: Passage: Agent Kavya noticed that the 'courier' wore shiny, spotless shoes on a muddy Cherrapunji morning. She smiled, handed him an empty envelope, and quietly alerted her team. What clue gave the 'courier' away?
steps: The morning was muddy, so anyone walking outside would have muddy shoes.
His shoes were shiny and spotless.
So he was probably not who he claimed to be.
example.answer: His spotless shoes on a muddy morning showed he was not a real courier.

learn.reallife: Detective and spy stories, from Byomkesh Bakshi to Feluda, keep readers hooked by hiding clues in plain sight.

games.title: Complete the conditional
pairs: he would have caught the train.

games.title: Spy story check
items: Ausable looks like the glamorous spies in films.
He is fat and ordinary-looking, which disappoints Fowler.
Max carries a pistol when he meets Ausable.
'If I were you, I would apologise' is a second conditional.
Suspense is at the heart of spy stories.
'The Midnight Visitor' was written by Robert Arthur.

quiz.q: Who is Ausable in 'The Midnight Visitor'?
options: A secret agent who does not look like a typical spy
quiz.explain: Ausable is a fat, plain-looking secret agent.

quiz.q: Who is Fowler in 'The Midnight Visitor'?
options: A young writer who expected spies to be glamorous
quiz.explain: Fowler is a writer disappointed by Ausable's ordinary looks.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two visitors to the room

quiz.q: Who is waiting in Ausable's room with a pistol?
quiz.explain: Max, a rival agent, has come for a secret paper.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the name of the villain

quiz.q: What story does Ausable invent to trick Max?
options: That the paper is in the kitchen
That Fowler is a police officer
That the hotel is on fire
That there is a balcony below the window
quiz.explain: He says there is a balcony and that police are coming, so Max will try to hide there.
quiz.mistake: Does not recall the key detail of the plan

quiz.q: Which is a typical feature of a spy story?
quiz.explain: Spy stories build suspense around secret missions.

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: 'If the police ___, they will search the room.'
quiz.explain: First conditional: If + present, will + verb.
quiz.mistake: Uses a past form in a first conditional

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: 'If I ___ a spy, I would carry a secret camera.'
quiz.explain: Second conditional for imaginary situations: If + past ('were').
quiz.mistake: Uses present tense for an imaginary situation

quiz.q: Passage: Agent Kavya noticed that the 'courier' wore shiny, spotless shoes on a muddy Cherrapunji morning. She smiled, handed him an empty envelope, and quietly alerted her team. What clue made Kavya suspicious?
options: His spotless shoes on a muddy morning
quiz.explain: Spotless shoes did not fit a muddy morning; she was the one who handed over the empty envelope.

teach.ask: Gappu: I want to be a spy bird! What makes a spy story exciting, and how do I say 'If I were a spy...'?
teach.praise: Agent Gappu reporting! Suspense, clues and a twist, and 'If I were a spy, I would...'. Top secret!
teach.nudge: What keeps readers excited in a spy story? And which verb follows 'If I' in an imaginary wish?

topics.title: Quick thinking: sequence words and story writing

learn.hook: One made-up balcony, one knock at the door, and a dangerous man is gone. That's thinking fast!
points: Ausable stays calm in danger. He invents a balcony below his window and tells Max the police are about to come.
When there is a knock, Max panics and climbs out onto the 'balcony', which does not exist. The knock was only a waiter bringing drinks Ausable had ordered.
Presence of mind means thinking calmly and quickly in an emergency; Ausable uses wit, not weapons.
Sequence words organise a story: first, then, next, after that, suddenly (for surprise), finally.
A good short story has a clear beginning, a problem, a turning point and an ending.

example.q: Put in sequence words: '___ the lights went out. ___ we heard footsteps. ___ the door creaked open. ___ it was only Dadi with a candle!'

learn.reallife: In a real emergency, like a power cut in a lift, staying calm and thinking clearly is the best help.

games.title: Build the story
items: Finally, we saw it was only Dadi with a candle.

quiz.q: How does Ausable get rid of Max?
options: He invents a balcony and says the police are coming
He fights him with a pistol
He gives him the secret paper
quiz.explain: His made-up story makes Max climb out of the window.
quiz.mistake: Thinks spies always win by fighting

quiz.q: Who was knocking at the door in 'The Midnight Visitor'?
quiz.explain: The knock was a waiter with the drinks Ausable had ordered.
quiz.mistake: Believes Ausable's bluff about the police

options: Thinking calmly and quickly in an emergency
quiz.explain: It is the ability to stay calm and act wisely in a crisis.

quiz.q: What does 'think on your feet' mean?
quiz.explain: It is an idiom for quick thinking in a situation.
Ausable bluffs about the balcony and the police.

quiz.q: Which word best signals a surprise in a story?
What does 'composed' mean when describing a person?
quiz.explain: A composed person stays calm, like Ausable.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only of the music meaning of 'compose'

quiz.q: Which action best shows quick thinking?
options: When the lift stopped, Neha started crying.
When the lift stopped, Neha tried to climb out of the roof.
When the lift stopped, Neha jumped up and down.
When the lift stopped, Neha pressed the alarm and calmly asked everyone to stay still.
quiz.explain: She stayed calm and did the safe, sensible thing.
quiz.mistake: Confuses dramatic action with quick, sensible thinking

teach.ask: Gappu: A cat was near my nest and I tricked it by chirping like a big hawk! Is that quick thinking like Ausable?
teach.praise: Hawk-chirp! Yes! Staying calm and using a clever trick is presence of mind, just like Ausable!
teach.nudge: Did you stay calm? What clever trick did you use instead of fighting?
